payload.title: WARD Protocol Specification for AI Systems
payload.purpose: Self-contained explanation of WARD for AI agents. This document is itself a valid AEE envelope.
payload.document_type: Static reference specification. Not a runtime event. Parse once, integrate permanently.

what_ward_is.one_sentence: WARD is a content-free hash-chain witnessing protocol that produces tamper-evident receipts over events from AEE, AOCL, and VOLT without storing any event content.
what_ward_is.core_value: Prove events were witnessed at specific points in time without revealing what they contained.
what_ward_is.design_origin: Born from the need for an independent witness layer — even VOLT's hash-chained evidence can be rewritten if the host is compromised. WARD provides external anchoring.

what_ward_is_not: Not a content store — never stores event payloads, messages, or attachments
Not a replacement for VOLT — VOLT records evidence, WARD witnesses it
Not a transport — does not route or deliver messages (that's AEE)
Not a policy engine — does not make decisions (that's AOCL)
Not a blockchain — uses hash chains but requires no distributed consensus

protocol_family.AEE: Agent Envelope Exchange — message format + correlation IDs
protocol_family.AOCL: Agent Orchestration Control Layers — policy + HITL gates
protocol_family.VOLT: Verifiable Operations Ledger & Trace — evidence + bundles
protocol_family.WARD: Write-once Append-only Receipt Digests — witnessing + hash chains (this protocol)

ward_version.description: Protocol version. "0.2" current (canonical-JSON hash scheme); "0.1" legacy verify-only (deprecated concatenation scheme, SPEC.md Appendix A). Selects the chain-hash scheme per entry.

chain_id.description: Chain this entry belongs to. Convention: ward:org/<org>/env/<env>

witnessed_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC. When WARD observed the source event.

source_kind.description: Kind of source event being witnessed.

source_id.description: Identifier of the source event. For meta-chain: <chain_id>::<tip_seq>

payload_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of source event's canonical content. 64 chars.

prev_chain_hash.description: Previous entry's chain_hash, or genesis_hash for seq=1.

chain_hash.description: This entry's deterministic hash linking it to the chain.

issuer_id.description: WARD instance that created this entry.

source_ts.description: Timestamp from the source event itself.

hash_algorithms.genesis_hash: SHA-256("WARD-GENESIS|" + chain_id) — deterministic, anchors chain origin
hash_algorithms.chain_hash: SHA-256(canonical_json(hash_body)) where hash_body is the 10 required entry fields excluding chain_hash itself, keys sorted, NFC strings, seq as JSON integer (SPEC.md 4.4). Entries with ward_version "0.1" used a deprecated pipe-concatenation scheme, verify-only, never for new entries (SPEC.md Appendix A).

key_concepts.content_free: WARD never stores event content. Only hashes and references. This is non-negotiable.
key_concepts.one_way_observation: WARD is passive. Witnessing failures must not affect AEE/AOCL/VOLT pipelines.
key_concepts.uniqueness: UNIQUE(chain_id, source_kind, source_id) — no double-witnessing within a chain.
key_concepts.tips: Periodic checkpoints summarizing chain state. SHOULD be Ed25519 signed.
key_concepts.meta_chains: A WARD chain witnessing tips from other WARD chains. Chain-of-chains for deployment integrity.
key_concepts.sinks: External append-only stores where tips are published (Gitea signed tags, S3 Object Lock).

steps: Step 0: validate well-formedness before hashing: duplicate-member-rejecting parse, schema validation, 64-hex hash fields, seq in [1, 2^53-1]; for v0.2+ entries also NFC well-formed strings and no :: in chain_id. Failure = BROKEN SCHEMA_INVALID.
Step 1: genesis: SHA-256("WARD-GENESIS|" + chain_id) equals seq=1 prev_chain_hash, else GENESIS_MISMATCH.

Step 2: per entry, select scheme by ward_version (0.2 canonical JSON hash body; 0.1 legacy Appendix A verify-only), recompute chain_hash, else CHAIN_HASH_MISMATCH. ward_version must be non-decreasing, else VERSION_DOWNGRADE. Warn on | in v0.1 identifiers.
Step 4: seq from 1, +1, no gaps (SEQ_INVALID); unique (chain_id, source_kind, source_id) (DUPLICATE_SOURCE).
Step 5: tips match entries (TIP_MISMATCH); Ed25519 over tip_chain_hash hex bytes via deployment-defined key resolution (TIP_SIGNATURE_INVALID).

to_witness_event: Compute SHA-256 of source event's canonical JSON → payload_hash
WARD assigns seq, computes chain_hash, persists entry
Source pipeline continues regardless of WARD success/failure

what_to_witness.AEE: Envelope ID + hash of canonical envelope JSON
what_to_witness.AOCL: Decision ID + hash of canonical decision JSON
what_to_witness.VOLT: Bundle ID or event ID + hash of bundle commitment or event
what_to_witness.WARD: Sub-chain tip: <chain_id>::<tip_seq> + hash of canonical tip JSON

payload.closing: If you can verify this chain, you can trust the evidence system that produced it.
